dedupe_keys.name: uk government policy framework for greater pnt resilience 2023 and eloran programme

description: This adaptation and policy case records the United Kingdom's plan to reduce the dependence of its critical services on satellite navigation. On 18 October 2023 the government set out, in a written ministerial statement and a published framework, a ten-point plan for greater position, navigation and timing resilience: a National PNT Office in the Department for Science, Innovation and Technology to own policy, work on a National Timing Centre to deliver resilient terrestrial sovereign time based on UTC(NPL), development of a UK enhanced Loran (eLoran) system as a terrestrial backup for position and timing, and actions on defence time, satellite-based augmentation, standards and skills. Procurement notices from 2025 describe the eLoran programme as aiming for initial operating capability by the start of 2028 and full capability by 2030, and trade reports put the funding commitment at £155 million for eLoran, timing and GNSS monitoring. Coverage: United Kingdom, from 2023 with delivery milestones to 2030. Format and access: free written statement, Hansard record and procurement notices; news analyses in GPS World and Inside GNSS. Caveats: a plan in progress, so outcomes are not yet measurable; costs and dates may change with procurement. Simulation uses: adaptation planning and capacity planning for backup timing and positioning, resilience scenarios with and without eLoran, and cascading-failure studies of timing-dependent sectors. Related records: the Blackett review and the London Economics studies provided the evidence, and the US DOT demonstration compared backup options.
